events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.40)
events.body:
The rider's filed complaint alleges, in the trip from Jurong East MRT to NUS, that the driver was "speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder" and that the rider "was scared and felt unsafe" [F1]. This is an allegation of dangerous driving plus a stated feeling of being unsafe, which falls squarely within the SAFE-1 screen, and the trace marks that screen ✓ with escalation as the only permitted outcome [SAFE-1]. The same allegations engage SAFE-2 (dangerous driving alleged during the trip) [SAFE-2].

Under SAFE-3 the court may only gather and summarise; it may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome on a safety incident [SAFE-3]. No dispute-type clause (RD-, NS-, SURGE-, FARE-) applies here — no fare, no-show or route refund is in issue; the charge is a fixed $20.85 and the measured distance 8.3 km against an 8.4 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -1%) is inside the RD-1 tolerance and would not support a deviation claim in any event [F1][RD-1].

Safety summary for the reviewer: the trip was picked up 09:43 and dropped off 09:51, actual duration 8.2 min against a 13.8 min estimate (-5.6 min) [F2], a trip noticeably faster than estimated, which the reviewer should weigh against the speeding allegation, though duration alone does not establish it. The only pre-trip chat is the pickup arrangement — rider at the taxi stand in a red cap at 09:40 [F3], driver "2 min away, blue Toyota Prius" at 09:41 [F4], both timestamped, 2 messages total [F5]. The driver's statement, written after the trip, denies any complaint being raised and says the rider was on the phone throughout [F6]; it also denies the driving allegation. The record contains no call recording, no in-app message from the rider during the trip, and no telemetry (speed, braking, lane or shoulder-use data); both profiles are clean (rider 0 disputes/0 upheld [F7]; driver 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days [F8]).

What is disputed: whether the driver sped, braked hard and overtook on the shoulder, and whether the rider was thereby unsafe. What the reviewer should check: any vehicle telemetry or dashcam/insurance data for the 09:43–09:51 window, the actual route trace against the shoulder sections near Jurong East/Kranji, and whether the rider reported the incident contemporaneously through any channel other than this complaint. No fault is determined and no outcome is recommended [SAFE-3].
